sm: A Tazewell Circuit Court held a five-hour hearing on a pro-life lawsuit seeking to block certification of a Virginia constitutional amendment, approved by voters on November 3, that would permit abortion throughout pregnancy. Judge Jack Hurley is scheduled to rule December 4 on four motions: venue, sovereign immunity, whether the complaint states valid claims, and a preliminary injunction. The Founding Freedoms Law Center filed the case for the Association of American Physicians and Surgeons, the Virginia Medical Freedom Alliance and Bluefield council member Meagan Kade. They argue the amendment is procedurally defective, since all parties agreed House Clerk Paul Nardo failed to send copies to local clerks for posting, and that the ballot question misled voters. Defendants said lawmakers later fixed this by changing the law retroactively. Josh Hetzler and Olivia Gans Turner criticized the process and ballot language. The amendment received about 63 percent of the vote.
